% note: All times are UTC. The lock tag times, and the commit times of the puzzle sets, Addendum C4, the record merge and the price-date commit, are git's tagger and committer times, as re-read from git in our final fact-check; the commit times of the length pick and of Study~1's k.json are from our own process record; run times are from our records of each run (a logged span starts when the run's command started, before its first call); the exposure scan's time is the Lock~4 manifest's; posting, snapshot and archive times are the public records' own. A date is printed on the first row of each UTC day; the rows below it fall on the same day. A row with no time is a ruling, or a run or step whose record gives only its date; it sits in order between the rows around it.
% note: Deviation~1's ruling has no recorded time: our decision records give only its date, with no time or time zone. That date, printed beside it, is a local calendar date, not a UTC one. It was ruled after the effort diagnostic and before the puzzle sets were committed.
% note: Run rows give each run's span from its records; the second panel splits it into invocations, the run's start, pauses, first call and last commit or end. ``Run started'' is the time our cost records log as the run's ``window started'' (after its first invocation). The top-up's ``First call'' is a dash: its work log records ``Window started'' and then its first batch of requests as sent, with no time for that send. Commits, postings and hashes are shortened in the timeline; the lock panel prints each lock's full commit ID and tar SHA-256, and ⟦TAB-23⟧ the analysis files' hashes.
% note: Study~1b's later invocations each re-submitted the 12-step point after its upload failed: waves w6--w8 (the 12-step point) failed to upload, and no batch was created; they were closed at \$0, and the 12-step point went through on its 4th attempt, a disclosed deviation (⟦TAB-19⟧).
% note: Lock~3's archive record v3: our project log records the DataCite registration at 13:28:29 UTC and the publication time read from the archive's API at 13:28:28 UTC; both fall inside the main run.
% note: Our lock procedure set an archive record plus a public posting with an archived snapshot as each lock's public proof; Lock~1 has all three. Lock~2 has only its archive record. Lock~3 was first public as a posting, with archive record v3 deposited during the main run, as its record states.
% note: Study~1b ran at the tag's only first-parent child; the top-up at a later commit that also moved the plan's earliest start time earlier, as a disclosed change (⟦TAB-19⟧).
% note: Exposed-puzzle sensitivity (third panel): a pre-registered sensitivity analysis. It is reported outside the main text (the paper's Appendix~D; here, ⟦TAB-10⟧'s sensitivity panel, which gives its $d$, 95\% interval, $p$ and error-rate ratio) and never replaces the primary result. Readings in quotation marks are the Study~1b file's own template words; the ruled reading, shown no worse (Holm-adjusted), is in the columns headed ``Shown no worse (Holm-adjusted)''.
% note: A dash: the records give nothing for that cell; in the lock panel, Lock~2's dash means it has no archived snapshot.
% note: Lock panel, last column: the next paid data after each lock, as our final fact-check lists it: the first call of Pilot~1, of the length sweep and of the main run (the main run's entry runs on to its last commit), and Study~1b's first invocation. The timeline's run rows instead start each run's span when its command started.
% note: Anonymous copy for review: the public proofs are fingerprints posted publicly before each study's runs; identifiers withheld for review, given at camera-ready (commit IDs and SHA-256 fingerprints are kept).
